evidence.title: The Private Life of Genghis Khan
evidence.description:
"The Private Life of Genghis Khan" is a short story written by Douglas Adams and Graham Chapman. It is based in part on a sketch devised by Graham Chapman, and written by Chapman and Adams for the 1975 TV show pilot Out of the Trees.[1] It appears in The Utterly Utterly Merry Comic Relief Christmas Book and some versions of The Salmon of Doubt. It is also available on Douglas Adams' website.[2]

Wowbagger, the Infinitely Prolonged (a recurring character from some of Adams' novels) makes a brief appearance in the story

truth_claims.note: conf=0.9; Standalone comic short story (1986), co-written by Douglas Adams and Graham Chapman from a sketch for the 1975 pilot "Out of the Trees"; EPUB metadata credits Adams alone. Published in The Utterly Utterly Merry Comic Relief Christmas Book and included in some editions of The Salmon of Doubt; also posted on douglasadams.com. ISFDB lists it as a standalone SHORTFICTION title with no series. It features a cameo by Wowbagger the Infinitely Prolonged from Life, the Universe and Everything, which links it loosely to the Hitchhiker's Guide universe, but no source assigns it a position in that (or any) numbered series, so reported as standalone.

truth_claims.note: conf=0.93; Standalone comic short story (1986), derived from a sketch for the 1975 TV pilot 'Out of the Trees'. Co-written with Graham Chapman, though ISFDB, Goodreads and the EPUB metadata all credit Douglas Adams alone; Chapman should be regarded as co-author. First published in 'The Utterly Utterly Merry Comic Relief Christmas Book' (1986) and later included in some editions of 'The Salmon of Doubt'; also posted on douglasadams.com. SERIES = NULL: although Wowbagger the Infinitely Prolonged (from Hitchhiker's) cameos at the end, ISFDB does NOT assign this title to the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy series — in its contents listing for 'The Salmon of Doubt' the neighbouring 'Young Zaphod Plays It Safe' carries the [Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy] series tag while this story carries none. A cameo does not make it a series volume, and it has no series number in any source.
